column1: # Expected seconds per runner test file, for runner/test/run.sh --shard (lib/shard.mjs
# balances the shards with these). seconds<TAB>file. Source: CI run 41154291906 (main
# at 692cf14), the median of the two macOS samples per file (the node 22 3-shard and
# node 24 2-shard cells; every file ran once in each), on macOS runners under -j 3 or
# -j 5 (the CPU count varies by runner), rounded, floor 1. The ubuntu cells (-j 4)
# ran the slow tests at 0.9-2x these times, in much the same order. Only the ratios
# A test missing here counts 10s; a line for a deleted test is ignored.
# Refresh a line when a test gets much slower or faster — an off weight only unbalances
# the shards, it never drops or duplicates a test.
# memory-index-after-merge, rework-cost-live, export-under-load: ESTIMATES, not CI
# medians (refresh them from the next CI run). Linux, alone: 70s / 36s / 9s; under load
# memory-index-after-merge took 156s where merge-lane took 249s against its 171 here,
# and the three are scaled by that ratio (rework-cost-live rounded up).
# e2e-release-gate-merge-typecheck: ESTIMATE too. Linux, one at a time under shared
# load: 131s where e2e-release-gate-merge-combination took 103s against its 100 here.
